manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pour all the water from the bowl on the left into the bowl on the right.

Task description: The light-blue bowl on the left currently contains water, and the light-blue bowl on the right is empty. Transfer the water from the left bowl into the right bowl without spilling it on the table.

Success criteria: Nearly all water from the left bowl has entered the right bowl, the left bowl is nearly empty, and no water has spilled onto the table.

## Execution tips

- The left bowl has no handle. Consider gripping the wall below the rim and above the water with one finger inside and one outside, away from the pouring edge toward the right bowl. Match the opening to wall thickness and approach clearance, ensuring pad contact to reduce slippage and preserve pouring room.
- Confirm the wall is actually between the fingers rather than merely overlapping in the image. Adjust while the bowl retains table support, test with a small lift and restore support before regrasping if it slides.
- Keep the water bowl opening upward and move smoothly; pause briefly if the liquid visibly sloshes to reduce spilling over the rim.
- Position the left bowl's pouring edge above the right opening's interior, preserving rim clearance and minimizing drop height. Adjust tilt incrementally while observing the stream landing point to avoid bowl collisions, splashing or overshooting the right bowl.
- Near empty, slowly increase tilt and pause briefly to let residual water gather at the pouring edge. If the stream nears the right bowl rim, reduce tilt before fine position adjustment, avoiding large movements while water continues flowing.

The right bowl moved slightly just now, possibly from contact as the bowls approached each other. I stopped the lateral approach and raised the left bowl. Next I will increase the clearance before continuing to pour at a small angle.
